claims.text: This package may read, prompt, record and verify. It has no writing, editing, applying or promotion capability anywhere, by construction rather than by promise
claims.why: This chunk only re-exports bus functions; it does not define or forbid write/edit/apply/promote operations. The claim is about the whole package, not observable here.

claims.text: The same structural property spine/attempt.py earned with 'THERE IS NO APPLY PATH'
claims.why: No spine/attempt.py code is in this chunk; the referenced property cannot be verified.

claims.text: A council's product is a queue of CHECKS for the existing deterministic gate (tests, fences, diffs) to run; the gate's result is the only verdict
claims.why: No gate, checks, or product-construction code appears in this chunk; this is a package-level behavioural claim.

claims.text: Dissent is recorded verbatim and is never averaged away
claims.why: The transcript functions (append_turn etc.) are re-exported but their implementation is in bus.py, not here; verbatim recording and averaging behaviour cannot be observed.

claims.text: Nothing in this package carries an approve / reject / score / majority / consensus / confidence field
claims.why: This chunk defines no fields at all; whether any symbol in the package carries such fields is not determinable from this file alone.

claims.text: Advisory-by-docstring is not a control; ABSENCE OF THE FIELD is the control
claims.why: This is a design principle stated in the docstring; no code in this chunk implements or contradicts it.

claims.text: FALSIFICATION PROTOCOL (stated in advance, before any wiring) -- The premise ... is plausible and UNTESTED. It is measured before session.py is wired into any real review workflow, and the module is deleted if it fails
claims.why: No session.py or measurement/wiring code exists in this chunk; cannot verify that measurement precedes wiring or that deletion would happen.

claims.text: ARM A: four vendors (anthropic / openai / google / local), one round each
claims.why: No vendor configuration or round logic in this chunk.

claims.text: CONTROL: ONE vendor asked twice under two different role prompts
claims.why: No control logic or role-prompt handling in this chunk.

claims.text: GROUND TRUTH: spine.attempt.GateResult.passed and AttemptResult.state -- already recorded, free to harvest
claims.why: No spine.attempt code or data harvesting in this chunk; the referenced symbols are not present.

claims.text: INDEPENDENCE: pairwise agreement rate BETWEEN vendors versus WITHIN one vendor across two calls
claims.why: No agreement-rate computation in this chunk.

claims.text: FALSIFIER: if inter-vendor agreement is within noise of intra-vendor agreement on N patches, THIS MODULE IS DELETED
claims.why: No deletion logic or agreement comparison in this chunk.

claims.text: SMALL-N CAVEAT, stated in advance: the independent corpus is ~17-20 tasks
claims.why: No corpus size or task list in this chunk.

claims.text: bus.py -- the transcript: an append-only, hash-chained, offline-verifiable dcouncil/1 store at runs/council/<council_id>.jsonl
claims.why: The store format, path, and hash-chaining are implemented in bus.py; this chunk only re-exports functions and constants. The path pattern runs/council/<council_id>.jsonl is not asserted here.

claims.text: It is a SEPARATE store from the memory ledger and shares no code path with it
claims.why: No memory-ledger code or shared-path analysis is possible from this chunk.

claims.text: Council turns are model chatter, and promoting model chatter to certified memory (three agreeing turns is three confirmations) is the fabrication failure this project treats as the worst one
claims.why: No memory-promotion logic or turn-count rule in this chunk.

claims.text: COUNCIL RECORDS ARE NEVER AN INPUT TO MEMORY RECALL
claims.why: No memory-recall code in this chunk; cannot verify the input policy.

The __all__ list matches the imported names exactly, so re-exports are consistent within this file.
The docstring asserts a structural no-write property, but this file itself does not enforce it; enforcement, if any, lives in bus.py and other modules. The claim is uncheckable here, not broken.
